claims.heading: Even numbers
claims.statement: \label{def:even} A natural number $n$ is \emph{even} if $n = 2k$ for some natural number $k$. The \emph{triangular number} $T_n$ is $T_n = 0 + 1 + \dots + n$.
claims.title: Even numbers

claims.heading: Closure under addition
claims.statement: \label{thm:even-add} If $a$ and $b$ are even natural numbers, then $a + b$ is even.
claims.title: Closure under addition

claims.statement: \label{prop:pred} Every natural number is strictly greater than its predecessor $n - 1$.
claims.status: refuted as printed; corrected statement proved

claims.statement: \label{rem:pred} With truncated subtraction $0 - 1 = 0$, Proposition~\ref{prop:pred} fails at $n = 0$; it holds for every $n \ge 1$.

claims.heading: Uniform bound
claims.statement: \label{thm:bound} There is a constant $C$, independent of $n$, such that $T_n \le C n^2$ for every natural number $n$.
claims.title: Uniform bound

claims.statement: \label{cor:even-triangle} For every natural number $n$, the triangular number $T_{4n}$ is even.
\label{rem:history} The identity of Theorem~\ref{thm:triangle} is traditionally attributed to Gauss.
